description: Concrete software-architecture capabilities that controls require (Layer 7). Implementations may extend; published reference patterns live alongside the source enum.

terms.definition: Centralised role-/attribute-based policy decision point used by every protected resource.
Append-only audit log with tamper-evident hash chain and an export endpoint.
Identity layer that carries tenant context on every request and is enforced at the PEP.
Programmable multi-party approval gates (e.g. four-eyes) with full audit of approver identity and time.
Authenticated endpoint that produces evidence artefacts in their canonical schema on demand.
Policy-driven retention, archival and legal-hold over log stores with verifiable enforcement.
Storage-level encryption with managed keys covering all in-scope data stores.
TLS (or equivalent) on all network paths carrying in-scope data, with modern cipher suites enforced.
Automated key generation, rotation and retirement on a documented cadence.
Centralised, access-audited store for secrets, credentials and signing keys.
Executable runbooks for incident detection, classification, response and post-incident review.
Inventory of AI systems with lifecycle state, risk classification, owner and required disclosures.
Pipeline that publishes structured model cards on release and on material change.
Production monitor for data, concept or performance drift, with documented thresholds and response.
Data-loss-prevention or redaction at egress paths for in-scope sensitive data.
Federated single-sign-on with enforced multi-factor authentication for all privileged or in-scope access.
Automated joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle via SCIM or equivalent identity provisioning.
Customer-controlled key (BYOK) or cloud (BYOC) options for in-scope data at rest.
Recorded provenance of data flows from source through processing to consumer, queryable for audit.
